referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width split-leaning hero with brand logo at top, large centered headline, short supporting line, and a compact benefit list using tick icons; primary conversion focus is immediate and above the fold.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-column editorial flow with stacked product sections; each section uses a label/kicker, strong headline, short descriptive paragraph, then a feature grid/list beneath. Visual rhythm is linear and content-led rather than modular dashboard-like.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Primarily simple feature blocks with minimal framing, no visible glassmorphism or heavy shadow treatment; cards appear utilitarian, text-forward, and evenly spaced.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA is prominent in the hero; form-based lead capture acts as the main conversion mechanism. Secondary CTAs are not emphasized in the extracted structure.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern detected in the provided structure.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not present in the extracted reference structure.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Light media usage focused on logo and small inline icons; no strong hero image, product mockup, or media panel pattern detected in the provided snippet.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Repeatable feature-section blocks with label, headline, supporting copy, and 4-5 feature items. Section hierarchy favors sequential reading and scannable benefit discovery over deep interactivity.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form card placed directly after the hero, visually separated as the main conversion module. Form appears structured for multiple hidden tracking fields plus visible lead inputs, suggesting a high-intent gated workflow.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static and conversion-oriented; no obvious animated transitions, counters, sliders, or reveal effects in the provided markup.
designNotes: Use a clear top-to-bottom conversion funnel: hero, form, then feature proof.
Keep copy blocks short and scannable; prioritize headings and bullet-like feature items.
Maintain generous whitespace and simple alignment to preserve an editorial B2B feel.
Favor utility over decoration: minimal borders, restrained icon use, and strong text hierarchy.
This reference is best suited for lead-generation landing pages where the form is a primary action, not a secondary one.

personality.buyer: Administrators, IT teams, and MSSPs managing firewall logs, traffic visibility, compliance, and incident investigation
personality.emotion: Controlled, vigilant, and highly trustworthy — built to feel operationally precise, audit-ready, and calm under pressure
personality.reasoning: Firewall Analyzer is a security operations product, so the visual language should communicate authority, monitoring precision, and compliance confidence rather than generic SaaS friendliness. The brand palette must come exclusively from Techjockey’s orange-led identity, so the design uses a deep charcoal-and-white operational base with the brand orange as the primary active signal. That creates a distinct cybersecurity feel while staying tied to the marketplace brand. The page should feel like a live command surface: dense information architecture, strong grid logic, alert-style chips, layered dashboard visuals, and premium motion that reinforces real-time monitoring and forensic control.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The hero headline is 8 words, so it needs a strong but compact size to maintain authority without overcrowding the split layout.

colours.colourReason: Primary CTA and hero background must use Techjockey’s brand orange per rules. To keep the page security-focused and visually distinct, the rest of the system leans on white, charcoal, and soft grey surfaces. The dark accent is used for contrast, section anchors, and data emphasis, while hover state shifts slightly deeper orange for premium responsiveness.

layout.heroBackground: Brand-orange hero with white text and a layered dashboard preview on the right
layout.heroReason: The product benefits from a split hero because firewall monitoring is best communicated with a live UI/dashboard visual rather than text alone. The orange hero makes the page instantly recognizable as Techjockey while signaling urgency, action, and operational momentum. Right side should show an abstract firewall analytics console, floating metric chips, and log-line overlays to suggest real-time surveillance.
layout.featureReason: There are many product capabilities, so tabs create a premium, interactive way to group functionality by use case: monitoring, analytics, compliance, and policy management. This prevents the page from feeling dense while giving administrators a sense of control and depth.
layout.darkSectionFor: Use a dark charcoal treatment only for the hero overlay layers, proof metrics strip, and a mid-page authority band featuring compliance/reporting highlights. This adds contrast without turning the entire page into a dark SaaS template.

personality.imageryDirection: Use a premium firewall dashboard composite rather than literal stock imagery: layered UI panels, network traffic graphs, log tables, alert badges, and device compatibility chips. The visual should feel like a live SOC console with clean data density, subtle glow on critical metrics, and small SVG icons for status, policy, audit, and bandwidth. If product screenshots are unavailable, build a CSS-based synthetic interface with grid overlays, terminal-like log strips, and performance cards.
personality.designPersonality: An audit-ready security control room: precise, structured, and quietly premium. The page should feel like a trusted network operations tool with strong brand-orange energy, crisp typography, layered dashboard depth, floating evidence chips, and clear visual hierarchy built for IT administrators and MSSPs.

Position as the deeper evaluation section. Keep cards consistent with section 1 for rhythm, but slightly more outcome-oriented in copy emphasis around compliance, dashboards, and change management.
Treat as a supporting differentiation section. Use concise cards and maintain visual consistency. Emphasize ROI, deployment simplicity, and reporting versatility.

layoutStrategy.hero: Use a strong centered or slightly split-leaning hero with dark security-themed background, white text, and a visible primary CTA. Include a short benefit list with tick icons to reinforce immediate value.
layoutStrategy.features: Use stacked, editorial product sections with label, headline, short supporting paragraph, and uniform feature cards. Keep the grid simple, utilitarian, and highly scannable; avoid interactive patterns like tabs or carousels.
layoutStrategy.proof: Place trust content early, then testimonials after feature depth to reinforce credibility. Use straightforward quote cards with visible attribution and minimal decoration.
layoutStrategy.pricing: No pricing section should be designed because no pricing data is present in the input.
layoutStrategy.form: No lead form should be designed because includeForm is false in context. Keep conversion oriented toward CTA clicks rather than gated capture.

designIntent.tokenProfileHint: Security product profile: use Rajdhani for headings and Inter for body copy. designIntent.figmaReadySummary: Design a single-product security landing page with a strong above-the-fold CTA, early trust reinforcement, and three sequential feature sections that progressively explain firewall compatibility, monitoring, compliance, and operational value. Keep the page structured, technical, and easy to scan for IT administrators and MSSPs. Avoid pricing and lead-form modules because the input does not provide them. Use consistent card-based feature presentation, minimal ornamentation, and high-clarity typography for a dependable enterprise feel.
